title: Recreating a childhood hex-capture game with modern fluid physics and different AI personalities. Here is how "Substrate: Core Ascension" turned out.
author: LordKrehn
selftext:
Growing up, I spent a lot of hours playing a hex-based node-capture strategy game that was part of a game bundle I've never been able to find. I can't even remember what the game was called.

I’ve been rebuilding that classic game to the best of my memory in Godot around two core rules:

* **Flow:** No units, no build queues. You just drag arrows between hexes to direct nanite ferrofluid. Point several arrows at one node to break a defense, or pull back to hold a chokepoint.
* **Liquid is conserved:** Zero fluid is created out of thin air. You grow by converting neutral nodes or draining rivals, so every push leaves a weak spot somewhere else.

**Current Features & Systems:**

* **10 CPU Personalities:** AI behaviors ranging from *Turtle* (defensive hoarders) and *Raider* (line cutters) to *Kingslayer* (punishes the leader). You can even build your own personalities.
* **Game Modes:** Free-for-all, Teams, and *Assassination* (secret hunt loops where your hunter isn't named like Rise of Nations).
* **Dynamic Feedback:** Off-screen threat alerts (press Tab to jump), overfilled hex glows, and a live SimCity-style news ticker tracking match events.

**Built with Godot + Claude AI** I recorded the entire development process as a tutorial series—writing the design doc, liquid physics, CPU logic, and UI step-by-step inside the Godot 4 editor using Claude AI. Feel free to ask for a link if you're interested.

**Free Download:** [https://rkrehn.itch.io/substrate-core-ascension](https://rkrehn.itch.io/substrate-core-ascension)
